Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:10:1.hebrew: והא זה וזה קתני - גבי מצאתיה תנא זה אומר, וגבי כולה שלי קתני זה אומר. ואי חדא הוא, הכי אבעי ליה למתני: זה אומר מצאתיה וכולה שלי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:10:1.english: But doesn't it teach "this [one]" and "this [one]"? - Regarding "I found it," [the tanna] taught: "This one says," and regarding "All of it is mine," he taught: "This one says." And if it were one [claim], this is what he should have taught: "This one says: I found it and all of it is mine."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:11:1.hebrew: במקח וממכר - קניתיה מיד פלוני. ודוקא מקח וממכר הוא דאמרינן יחלוקו בשבועה, דאיכא למימר שניהם קנאוה ולשניהם נתרצה המוכר. אבל זה אומר אני ארגתיה וזה אומר אני ארגתיה, לא יחלוקו, דודאי חד מינייהו רמאי הוא, ותהא מונחת עד שיבא אליהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:11:1.english: In [a case of] buying and selling - [Each claims:] "I bought it from so-and-so." And specifically [in a case of] buying and selling do we say that they divide it upon [taking] an oath, for it can be said that both of them bought it and the seller agreed [to sell] to both of them. But [if] this one says, "I wove it," and that one says, "I wove it," they do not divide it, for one of them is certainly a deceiver, and it shall be left until Elijah comes.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:1:1.hebrew: שנים אוחזין בטלית - דוקא אוחזין, דשניהם מוחזקים בה, ואין לזה כח בה יותר מזה. שאילו היתה ביד אחד לבדו, הוי אידך המוציא מחבירו, ועליו להביא ראיה בעדים שהיא שלו, ואינו נאמן זה ליטול בשבועה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:1:1.english: Two are holding a garment - Specifically [when they are] holding [it], for both of them are in possession of it, and this one has no greater claim to it than that one. For had it been in the hand of one [of them] alone, the other would be the one seeking to extract [property] from his fellow, and it would be upon him to bring proof through witnesses that it is his, and this [claimant] would not be believed to take [it] with an oath.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:1:2.english: This one says: "All of it is mine" - In the Gemara, it explains why [the Tanna] taught both [clauses].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:1:3.english: This one shall swear - The Gemara explains (3a) why this oath [is required].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:1:4.english: That he does not have in it less than half of it - In the Gemara (5b), it explains why they instituted this formulation for this oath.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:2:1.hebrew: וזה אומר חציה שלי - מודה הוא שהחצי של חבירו, ואין דנין אלא על חציה. הלכך, זה האומר כולה שלי ישבע כו' כמשפט הראשון: מה שהן דנין עליו, נשבעין שניהם שאין לכל אחד בו פחות מחציו, ונוטל כל אחד חציו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:2:1.english: And this one says: Half of it is mine - He concedes that half belongs to his fellow, and they litigate only over [the other] half. Therefore, [the ruling that] "the one who says: All of it is mine, shall swear, etc." is in accordance with the first ruling: Whatever they litigate over, both of them swear that neither of them has less than half of it, and each one takes half of it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:3:1.hebrew: היו שנים רוכבין כו' - לאשמועינן אתא, דרכוב ומנהיג שניהם שוין לקנות בהמה מן ההפקר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:3:1.english: [If] two were riding, etc. - It comes to teach us that [one who is] riding and [one who is] leading are both equal in acquiring an animal from ownerless property.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:4:1.english: When they admit - In the Gemara (8a), it explains that through this, it teaches us that one who lifts a found item for his fellow, his fellow acquires [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:6:1.english: I saw it - Before you picked it up.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:6:2.english: He acquires [it] through sight - From [the fact] that it teaches: "They shall divide [it]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:6:3.hebrew: תנא כולה שלי - בחזקה גמורה, שהגבהתי תחילה, ואתה תפסת מידי משזכיתי בה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:6:3.english: [The Tanna] taught: "All of it is mine" - [Meaning, he claims it] through complete acquisition: that "I lifted it first, and you seized it from my hand once I had acquired it."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:7:1.english: But didn't Rabbanai say - In Bava Kamma, in [the chapter] HaGozel U'Ma'akhil.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:7:2.hebrew: ומצאתה דאתא לידיה משמע - ואפילו הכי, אחיך ולא עובד כוכבים. ולא תימא: כי מיעט רחמנא עובד כוכבים, היכא דלא אתאי לידיה דישראל, לא מיחייב למטרח עלה ולאהדורה, אבל אתא לידיה, מיחייב להחזירה, דאבידתו אסורה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:7:2.english: "And you have found it" indicates that it came into his possession - And even so, [the verse states] "your brother," and not an idolater. And do not say that when the Merciful One excluded an idolater, [this means only that] where it did not come into the possession of a Jew, he is not obligated to trouble himself over it and return it, but [if] it came into his possession, he is obligated to return it, because [retaining] his lost property is forbidden.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:8:1.hebrew: תנא לישנא דעלמא נקט - אי לא הדר תנא כולה שלי, הוה אמינא: מאי מצאתיה דקתני? תנא לשון בני אדם אחז במשנתנו, ולא לשון מקרא, והרבה בני אדם קורין לה מציאה משעת ראיה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:8:1.english: The Tanna employed colloquial language - Had the Tanna not gone back and taught "All of it is mine," I would have said: What is [the meaning of] "I found it" that [the Tanna] taught? The Tanna adopted the language of ordinary people in our Mishnah, and not the language of Scripture, and many people call it a "find" from the moment of sighting.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:9:1.hebrew: בעלמא דקתני מצאתיה - בכ"מ ששנינו שהמוצא מציאה קנאה, הוה אמינא דמציאה קני לה משעת ראיה, דלא אשמעינן שום תנא דלא קני לה אלא בהגבהה. להכי אשמעינן הכא ממשנה יתירה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 2a:9:1.english: In general, where [the Tanna] teaches: "I found it" - In every place where we learned that one who finds a lost item acquires it, I would have said that he acquires a lost item from the moment of sighting, since no Tanna taught us that he acquires it only through lifting. For this reason, [the Tanna] taught us here from the superfluous [wording of the] Mishnah.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:10:1.hebrew: והא זה וזה קתני - איכא דוכתי דפריך כי האי גוונא, ואיכא דוכתי דלא פריך: [עי' תוס' בכורות דף לא: ד"ה א"כ]:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:10:1.english: But doesn't it teach "this one" and "this one"? - There are places where [the Gemara] raises a challenge of this sort, and there are places where it does not raise a challenge. [See Tosafot, Bekhorot 31b, s.v. Im ken].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:1:1.hebrew: שנים אוחזין בטלית - איידי דאיירי בהגוזל בתרא (ב"ק דף קיט.) מחלוקת נסורת נגר ובעל הבית, דקתני: במעצד הרי אלו שלו, ובכשיל הרי אלו של בעל הבית, תני הכא נמי דיני חלוקות. ואע"ג דבתרי מסכתא אין סדר למשנה, ואיכא מ"ד כולה נזיקין לאו חדא מסכתא הוא, ה"מ לענין מחלוקת ואח"כ סתם, לפי שרבי לא היה לומד כסדר אלא כמו שהיו חפצים התלמידים; אבל כשחברם, על הסדר חברם, וצריך בכל מסכתא טעם למה נשנית אחר שלפניה, כדדייק בריש מסכת שבועות (דף ב.): מכדי תנא ממכות קסליק כו', וכן בסוטה (דף ב.):
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:1:1.english: Two hold a garment - Since [the Tanna] dealt in [the chapter] HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 119a) with the division of shavings between the carpenter and the homeowner, as it teaches: "[If planed] with an adze, these belong to him [the carpenter], and with an axe, these belong to the homeowner," he teaches here too the laws of division. And even though across two tractates there is no [fixed] order to the Mishnah, and there is an opinion that the entire [order of] Nezikin is not a single tractate — this applies only regarding [the rule of] "a dispute and afterward an anonymous [mishnah]," because Rebbe did not teach in order, but rather according to what the students desired; however, when he compiled them, he compiled them in order, and in every tractate a reason is needed for why it was taught after the one preceding it, as [the Gemara] infers at the beginning of Tractate Shevuot (2a): "After all, the Tanna concluded [Makkot], etc.," and similarly in Sotah (2a).

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:1:2.hebrew: ויחלוקו - תימה: דמאי שנא מההיא דארבא, דאמר "כל דאלים גבר" פרק חזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף לד: ושם)? וי"ל, ד"אוחזין" שאני, דחשיב כאילו כל אחד יש לו בה בודאי החצי, דאנן סהדי דמאי דתפיס האי דידיה הוא. וכן במנה שלישי, דמדמי בגמרא לטלית, חשיב ההוא שהנפקד תופס בחזקת שניהם כאילו הם עצמם מוחזקים בו. לכך משני, דהתם ודאי דחד מינייהו הוא, ואין החלוקה יכולה להיות אמת, ולכך יהא מונח; אבל טלית, דאיכא למימר דתרוייהו הוא — יחלוקו. וכן שנים אדוקים בשטר, דמדמי לקמן (בבא מציעא דף ז.) למתני', משום דשניהם אדוקים בו, דהחלוקה יכולה להיות אמת, דאפשר שפרע לו החצי; ובמנה, אין דרך שיקנה לו החצי אחרי שהוא ביד חבירו. אבל בארבא, אע"ג דאפשר שהיא של שניהם, כיון דאין מוחזקין בו, הוי דינא "כל דאלים גבר". ולסומכוס, אע"ג דאין מוחזקין בו ואין החלוקה יכולה להיות אמת, היכא דאיכא דררא דממונא — פירוש: שבלא טענותיהם יש ספק לבית דין — יחלוקו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:1:2.english: And let them divide it - [This is] puzzling: For how is [this case] different from that [case] of the boat, where [the Gemara] says "Whoever is stronger prevails" in chapter Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 34b and there)? And it can be answered that [the case of two] holding [an item] is different, for it is considered as though each one definitely has [ownership of] half of it, as we are witnesses [i.e., it is evident to the court] that what this one is holding is his. And similarly regarding the third maneh, which the Gemara compares to the cloak, that which the bailee holds in the presumed possession of both of them is considered as if they themselves are in possession of it. For this reason [the Gemara] answers that there, [the third maneh] definitely belongs to [only] one of them, and the division cannot be the truth, and therefore it shall be left lying; but [by] a cloak, where it can be said that it belongs to both of them, they divide it. And similarly, [the case of] two who are grasping a promissory note, which [the Gemara] compares below (Bava Metzia 7a) to our Mishnah, [it is] because both of them are grasping it, where the division can be the truth, for it is possible that [the borrower] repaid him half; whereas in [the case of] the maneh, there is no way that one would transfer ownership of half to him after it is in the hand of his fellow. However, regarding the boat, even though it is possible that it belongs to both of them, since they are not in possession of it, the law is "Whoever is stronger prevails." And according to Sumkhos, even though they are not in possession of it and the division cannot be the truth, where there is an inherent monetary doubt [derara demamona] — meaning, that without their claims the court has a doubt — they divide it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:2:1.hebrew: וזה נוטל רביע - וא"ת: יהא נאמן דחציו שלו מיגו דאי בעי אמר כולה שלי, כדאמרי' בגמ' (לקמן בבא מציעא דף ח.) האי מיגו גופיה לפטרו משבועה, אי לא משום דאיערומי קמערים? ומפרש ריב"ם, דמיגו להוציא לא אמרי', דבחציו השני מוחזק זה כמו זה. וההיא דחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף לב: ושם), דגחין ולחיש ליה לרבה: אין, שטרא זייפא הוא, ומיהו שטרא מעליא הוה לי בידי ואבד, והימניה רבה להוציא במיגו דאי בעי אמר שטרא מעליא הוא - התם היינו טעמא, משום דאפי' הוה שתיק, רק שלא היה מודה שהוא מזוייף, היה נאמן, כי החתימה היתה נכרת לעומדים שם. ורב יוסף אית ליה דאפילו מיגו לא הוה, כיון שטענה ראשונה שהוא טוען בהאי שטרא הוא שקר; ואין לומר מיגו אלא היכא שטענתו ראשונה היא אמת, מיגו שהיה טוען אחרת, ולכך אינו מיגו אפילו להחזיק, כגון בעובדא קמייתא. וא"ת: ונימא דאין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי, דהאומר כולה שלי יש לו בודאי חציה, והאומר חציה שלי ספק אם יש לו בה כלום, כדאמרינן בפרק החולץ (יבמות דף לח.): ספק ויבם שבאו לחלוק בנכסי סבא, ספק אמר: אנא בר מתנא אנא ואית לי פלגא, ויבם אמר: את ברא דידי ולית לך ולא מידי, הוה ליה יבם ודאי וספק ספק, ואין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי? וי"ל, דהתם יבם, שהוא בנו של סבא, הוי ודאי יורשו, ולא יוציא הספק מספק ממונו; אבל הכא, אין סברא מה שהוא ודאי בחציו שיועיל לו לחציו השני:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:2:1.english: And this one takes a quarter - And if you say: Let him be believed that half of it is his by virtue of a *migo*, since if he wanted, he could have said "All of it is mine" — as we say in the Gemara (below, 8a): this *migo* itself [would serve] to exempt him from an oath, were it not that he is acting craftily? And the Ribam explains that we do not apply a *migo* to extract [property], for regarding the other half, this one is in possession just as that one [is]. And as for that [incident] in *Chezkas HaBatim* (Bava Batra 32b and ibid.), where [a person] bent down and whispered to Rabbah: "Yes, this deed is a forgery; however, I had a valid deed in my hand and it was lost," and Rabbah believed him to extract [the property] based on a *migo* that if he wanted, he could have said, "It is a valid deed" — there, the reason is that even had he remained silent, provided only that he did not admit that it was forged, he would have been believed, because the signature was recognizable to those standing there. And Rav Yosef holds that it was not even a *migo*, since the initial claim that he makes with this deed is false; and one does not apply a *migo* except where his initial claim is true, through a *migo* that he could have made a different claim. Therefore, it is not a *migo* even to retain possession, such as in the first incident. And if you say: Let us say that an uncertainty does not extract [property] from a certainty, for the one who says "All of it is mine" definitely has half of it, whereas regarding the one who says "Half of it is mine," it is uncertain whether he has anything in it at all — as we say in the chapter *HaCholetz* (Yevamot 38a): A *safek* [a person of uncertain parentage] and a *yavam* who came to divide the estate of the grandfather; the *safek* said, "I am the son of the deceased [brother], and I am entitled to half," and the *yavam* said, "You are my son, and you have nothing at all." The *yavam* is a certainty and the *safek* is an uncertainty, and an uncertainty does not extract from a certainty! And one can answer: There, the *yavam*, who is the son of the grandfather, is definitely his heir, and the *safek* cannot extract his property based on uncertainty; but here, there is no logic [to say] that the fact that he is certain regarding [his own] half should benefit him regarding the other half.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:6:1.hebrew: בראיה בעלמא קנה - אע"ג דקתני במתני' (לקמן בבא מציעא דף ט:) ראה את המציאה ואמר לחבירו תנה לי, דלא קנה בראיה; וכן ראה את המציאה ונפל עליה (לקמן בבא מציעא דף י.) קתני נמי דלא קני, מצי למדחי: כיון דאמר תנה לי או שנפל עליה, גלי דעתיה דלא ניחא ליה למקני עד שיגיע לידו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:6:1.english: Through mere sight he acquires [it] - Even though it teaches in the Mishnah (below, Bava Metzia 9b): "[If] one saw a found item and said to his fellow: 'Give it to me,'" that he did not acquire [it] through sight; and similarly, "[If] one saw a found item and fell upon it" (below, Bava Metzia 10a), it also teaches that he does not acquire [it] — [one] could reject [this]: Since he said "Give it to me," or fell upon it, he revealed his intention that he did not wish to acquire [it] until it reaches his hand.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:8:1.hebrew: דבראיה בעלמא לא קני - והא דאמרי' בפרק הבית והעלייה (לקמן בבא מציעא דף קיח. ושם) הבטה בהפקר קני, היינו שעשה מעשה כל דהו, כגון שגדר גדר קטן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 2a:8:1.english: That by mere sighting, one does not acquire - And that which we say in chapter HaBayit VeHaAliya (below, Bava Metzia 118a, and there), "Looking at ownerless property acquires [it]" — that is where he performed some minimal action, such as building a small fence.
